official_wording: Determine a text's purpose (e.g., to entertain, inform, or persuade) and its target audience.

proficient_ald: Determine the purpose and target audience of a text. (DRAFT ALD, Oct 2025, 3.T.C.1 Proficient)
what_is_taught: Teaches the three purposes (inform, persuade, entertain) with clue words, a "what does the whole text mostly do" check for directions, and audience clues (names, "you", what the reader is asked to do). Practice/test use a persuasive letter, a team welcome page and short stems.
other_demonstrations: R-OPN-01-5 (1 item, 1 pt: audience + purpose of an opinion text). No PT-1 item.
components: determine purpose: inform/persuade/entertain [taught+tested: P1,P4,P5,T1,T5]; determine target audience [taught+tested: P2,T2,T3,T5]; purpose+audience applied to a revision choice [tested: T4]
modal_requirements: None required beyond reading. Text-only is adequate.
evidence: T-C.js:3-197. Solved all 5 test items; keys correct. T1 "to help new players get ready" distractor "to get kids to sign up" is ruled out by "We are glad you joined us". T5 audience (students) is the only option pairing persuade + come to the fair. Site flag tested=reading matches blueprint 3.T.C.1(a) Interpreting. Site flag tested=reading agrees with the blueprint.

official_wording: Identify common text features in print, digital, auditory, spoken, and visual modes and explain how they contribute to purpose and effect.
source_ref: Georgia K-12 ELA Standards (2023), via js/data/standards.js line 1265
proficient_ald: Determine common text features [in] various text modes and describe how they contribute to the overall purpose and/or effect. (DRAFT ALD, Oct 2025)
what_is_taught: Teaches headings, bold words + glossary, text boxes, pictures/captions/diagrams/labels, and on-screen links, play buttons, video and sound, each with its job. Headings and "Did You Know?" boxes are real rendered features; every other feature is described in words ("Imagine a diagram...", "(The word stem is in bold.)").
other_demonstrations: R-INF-01-6 (1 pt, text box); PT-1-12 (1 pt, heading). Both are heading/box only.
components: identify/explain headings [taught+tested with real rendered headings: P1,P2,T1,T5]; text box [taught+tested, real: P3,T2]; bold word + glossary [taught+practiced P4 via description only; not tested; bold is never rendered]; diagram/labels [taught; P5,T3 use an imagined diagram described in a stem; no diagram is shown]; picture + caption [taught in teach points/example only; NOT practiced or tested]; digital mode: link, play button [tested T4 via description]; auditory mode: speaker button [practiced P7 via description]; spoken mode [not addressed]; contribution to purpose and effect [tested for headings/box/link; not for pictures/captions]
modal_requirements: Truly needs visual (pictures, captions, diagrams, bold print, maps) and digital/auditory modes. The site renders NO images, bold or media (assets/ is empty; SPEC.md:136 "The site shows no images"). Visual and digital features exist only as verbal descriptions the child must imagine. Milestones items show real photos, captions, diagrams and sidebars.
evidence: T-C.js:199-411. SK-TC1b-P5 (T-C.js:319) and SK-TC1b-T3 (T-C.js:370) stems begin "Imagine a diagram next to the article". SK-TC1b-T4 (T-C.js:389) describes a link and play button in text. No item of the lesson asks about a caption. js/engine/player.js renders "## " headings, "Box: " asides and "Caption: " lines only; no image element. Playwright on port 8441: 0 img/svg/canvas/video/audio in the skill page main area. Test keys verified correct (T1-T5). Site flag tested=reading agrees with the blueprint.
recommended_correction: Add real, original visuals (inline SVG or simple PNG drawn for the site, no GaDOE art): (1) a labeled diagram (e.g., beaver lodge cross-section) with a caption, used by P5 and a new test item; (2) a photo/drawing + caption item asking what the caption adds and which caption fits; (3) render bold via markup (e.g., **lodge**) in the passage so the bold item uses a real bold word with a glossary box; (4) one test item on caption purpose/effect. Update SPEC.md §5 rule "The site shows no images" to allow simple original visuals.
post_fix_note: 13 original figures/bold text added; captions, diagrams, bold and a spoken feature now taught; caption and diagram items practiced and tested (SK-TC1b-P5,P8,P9,T3,T6). Open: bold practiced but not tested; digital/audio features still described in words.

official_wording: Create multimodal texts using features of pre-selected modes for a specific purpose and audience.
source_ref: Georgia K-12 ELA Standards (2023), via js/data/standards.js line 1276
proficient_ald: Create multimodal texts, using features of pre-selected modes that are connected to a specific purpose and audience. (DRAFT ALD, Oct 2025)
what_is_taught: Teaches choosing pictures, captions, labels and sounds that match the words, purpose and audience of a poster or slide. Practice/test are selection items on two student plans (slide show, poster). A write activity asks the child to plan a poster in words.
other_demonstrations: Write activity (T-C.js:463): plan a poster for younger kids, describe one picture, write a caption, add a label or sound idea; 5-item grown-up checklist. No mixed-set or PT-1 items.
components: consider purpose and audience [taught+tested: T1,T4]; choose a fitting picture [taught+tested: P1,P4,T1]; write/choose a caption [taught+tested: P2,T2; written in write activity]; labels [taught+tested: P3,T5]; sound/auditory mode [taught+tested: P5,T3]; actually CREATE a multimodal text [only planned in words in the write box; the child never places a picture, draws, records or arranges a slide]
modal_requirements: Needs visual and possibly auditory creation. The site has no drawing, upload, image or audio capability; the write box asks the child to DESCRIBE a picture. Selection items match how Milestones would assess this, but creation itself is off-site and only implied.
evidence: T-C.js:413-604. All test keys verified. SK-TC1c-T4 (T-C.js:582) key "Make the title big so it is easy to see from far away" is reasonable design advice but is not taught in the lesson or grounded in the passage (minor). Write prompt: "Describe one picture you would draw." Site flag tested=writing agrees with the blueprint.
recommended_correction: Change the write activity to a hands-on make: "On paper, draw your poster: title, one picture, a caption and one label; read it to a grown-up." Add a coach/parent line telling the grown-up to check that picture, caption and label match the purpose and audience. Optionally add one teach point on layout/size (title big, one main picture) so SK-TC1c-T4 is grounded.
post_fix_note: Write activity now has the child draw and label a real picture on paper, write title/caption/facts, and add sound or present aloud (grown-up checks). Selection items unchanged.

official_wording: Describe the perspective of a narrator or speakers and distinguish it from one's own.

proficient_ald: Describe different perspectives of the narrator or speakers. (DRAFT ALD, Oct 2025, 3.T.C.2 Proficient)
what_is_taught: Teaches narrator vs. speaker (poem), finding the narrator's feeling words, first vs. third person, and comparing what the narrator says with what actually happens so the reader can hold a different view. Both lesson passages are first-person narrators whose view changes.
other_demonstrations: R-LIT-02-q1 (1 pt, narrator view); R-POE-01-q5 (2 pt, poem speaker's feeling); R-POE-01-q7 (1 pt, speaker vs. character); PT-1-6 (1 pt, narrator vs. Aunt Bea view).
components: describe the narrator's perspective [taught+tested: P2,P3,T2,T4]; describe a speaker's perspective (poem) [taught in teach point; practiced/tested only in R-POE-01-q5,q7, not in the lesson]; describe different perspectives (two characters) [learn 2; PT-1-6]; distinguish narrator's view from one's own [modeled as "a reader might see it differently": P3,T3,T5]; point of view first/third person [taught+tested: P1,P4,T1]
modal_requirements: None required. Oral discussion of the child's own view is suggested in the parent note.
evidence: T-C.js:606-787. All test keys correct; no giveaways. "Distinguish from one's own" is operationalized as "which detail might make a reader see it differently" (T3, T5), which is a fair test proxy. No third-person passage in the lesson, so third-person narrator perspective is only taught via the match item P4. Site flag tested=reading agrees with the blueprint.
recommended_correction: Optional: add one lesson item using a short poem with a speaker (the teach point already mentions speakers), and one third-person passage item.
post_fix_note: No change in PP-003 fix phase.

official_wording: With adult support, identify the context in which a text was written (time period, individual, situation).
source_ref: Georgia K-12 ELA Standards (2023), via js/data/standards.js line 1298
proficient_ald: No Proficient descriptor. Appears only at Distinguished: "Identify the context in which a text is written." (DRAFT ALD, Oct 2025)
what_is_taught: Teaches context clues (date, place, writer, box note), why time period matters, that different writers see things differently, and that historical fiction pretends to be from the past. Learn 2 models a situation (dry summer -> no-campfire sign). Practice and test use two historical-fiction pieces (1928 letter, 1954 diary).
other_demonstrations: None in mixed sets or PT-1.
components: time period [taught+tested: all P and T items]; individual (who wrote it and how that shapes it) [teach point only; not practiced or tested]; situation [learn 2 and teach example only; not practiced or tested]; with adult support [parent note]; how context aids understanding [tested: P5,T2,T4]
modal_requirements: None required.
evidence: T-C.js:789-981. All 10 items hinge on the time period (1928 / 1954). No item asks how the writer's identity (child, ranger, scientist) or the situation shapes the text, though teach point 3 and learn 2 introduce them. Keys verified correct. Site flag tested=reading agrees with the blueprint.
recommended_correction: Add one practice and one test item on "individual" (e.g., same event described by a park ranger vs. a child; which detail shows who wrote it) and one on "situation" (a sign or note written during an event; why it says what it says).
post_fix_note: Added SK-TC2c-P6 (individual) and SK-TC2c-T6 (situation, needs the context box). Open: 'individual' practiced not tested; 'situation' tested, only modeled in Watch Me.

official_wording: Describe how texts are arranged using text features (e.g., maps, captions) and organizational structures (e.g., cause/effect), referring to chapters or sections.
source_ref: Georgia K-12 ELA Standards (2023), via js/data/standards.js line 1309
proficient_ald: Describe how a text is arranged to represent information and ideas using text features and organizational structures. (DRAFT ALD, Oct 2025)
what_is_taught: Main lesson teaches the five structures with clue words, headings/sections, text boxes, captions and maps. Five structure lessons (TS-SEQ, TS-CE, TS-PS, TS-CC, TS-DESC) each teach one structure with clue words and an organizer; 3.T.T.1.b adds story structure. Maps and captions are only described in words.
other_demonstrations: R-INF-01-3 (2 pt), R-INF-01-4 (2 pt), R-INF-01-7 (1 pt), PT-1-11 (1 pt). Clue-word box with organizer to draw in all 7 lessons; coach boxes ("Teach it in 5 minutes"). Counts in the numeric columns are totals over 7 lessons (see notes for per-lesson split).
components: organizational structures: sequence, cause/effect, problem/solution, compare/contrast, description [taught+tested richly in TS-* and main lesson]; story structure [3.T.T.1.b lesson]; referring to sections [taught+tested: SS1a-P1,P3,T1,T2,T5]; referring to chapters [not addressed]; text features: headings, text box [taught+tested with real rendered features]; captions [tested only via an imagined photo: SS1a-T4]; maps [learn 3 and SS1a-P6 describe a map in words; no map shown, not tested]
modal_requirements: Maps and captions are named in the standard and need visuals. No map or captioned picture is ever displayed (site renders no images). Structures are fully served by text.
evidence: T-SS.js:9-231 plus T-TS.js (TS-SEQ:3, TS-CE:213, TS-PS:415, TS-CC:615, TS-DESC:824) and T-T1.js:207. All 35 test items solved; keys correct. Learn 3 (T-SS.js:84): "Next to the article is a map of Georgia with the river drawn in blue" (no map shown). SK-SS1a-T4 (T-SS.js:209) asks for a caption for a described photo. Note: the 3.T.T.1.b lesson lists 3.T.SS.1.a in codes but none of its items carry the 3.T.SS.1.a std tag (they default to 3.T.T.1.b). Site flag tested=reading agrees with the blueprint.
recommended_correction: Add one simple original map (e.g., Georgia outline with the Chattahoochee) to learn 3 and one test item that requires reading it; add one captioned picture item. Add one item that refers to a chapter (e.g., a table of contents with chapter titles: "In which chapter would you find..."). Shares the visuals fix recommended for 3.T.C.1.b.
post_fix_note: Real map figure in Watch Me; SK-SS1a-P6 peanut-farm map; SK-SS1a-T4 picture with caption; SK-SS1a-P7 table of contents/chapters.

source_ref: Georgia K-12 ELA Standards (2023), via js/data/standards.js line 1320
proficient_ald: Design a text using a variety of text structure(s) and features, according to purpose and audience. (DRAFT ALD, Oct 2025)
what_is_taught: Teaches choosing a plan for the job and reader: steps in order for how-to, sections with headings for a topic, features (heading, caption, numbered list), an opening and a closing. Practice/test are revising items on two student drafts; a write activity asks for a how-to piece.
other_demonstrations: Write activity (T-SS.js:288, how-to for a younger child, 5-item checklist). W-REV-02-8 (1 pt, feature for a family audience).
components: sequence structure for how-to [taught+tested: P1,T4]; topical sections + headings [taught+tested: P2,T2,T5]; other structures (compare, cause/effect) [practice match P5 only; not tested]; features: heading, caption, numbered list [taught+tested heading/caption: P3,T3; numbered list learn 3 only]; suited to audience [P3, learn 3, W-REV-02-8; no lesson test item turns on audience]; closing [P4]

recommended_correction: Replace or add one test item where the structure must be chosen for a non-sequence job (e.g., "Priya wants to explain how the old and new library are alike and different. Which plan fits?"), and one where the audience decides the feature (e.g., first graders vs. parents).
post_fix_note: Added SK-SS1b-T6 (audience decides design) and SK-SS1b-T7 (choose a compare plan); SK-SS1b-T1 (a 3.T.SS.1.d item) removed.

proficient_ald: Use conjunctions and transition words or phrases, such as although and since, to add cohesion and link ideas and information within a paragraph. (DRAFT ALD, Oct 2025)
what_is_taught: Teaches five linking words by job: because/since (reason), also (adds), although (surprise), for example (example), with a try-it-in-the-sentence strategy. Revising items on an opinion and an informational draft.
other_demonstrations: Write activity (T-SS.js:476). W-REV-01-2 (2 pt: First, / In addition,), W-REV-01-4 (1 pt: so), W-REV-02-5 (2 pt: This time, / A week later,), PT-1-15 (1 pt: Besides seeing well,). W-TASK-01/02 list 3.T.SS.1.c and the Writer's Checklist line on linking words.
components: conjunctions because/since/although [taught+tested in lesson]; coordinating conjunctions so/but/or [only in W-REV-01-4 and as distractors]; transition words/phrases for adding/example (also, for example) [taught+tested]; transitions for order and reasons (First, In addition, A week later, Besides...) Site flag tested=writing agrees with the blueprint.
